stories.title: PIA passengers in UK left distressed as 2 flights cancelled due to abrupt Norse Atlantic suspension
summary: Pakistan International Airlines (PIA) said on Wednesday it will move its UK operations to its own Boeing 777 fleet from Nov 26 after wet-lease partner Norse Atlantic Airways abruptly suspended operations, forcing the cancellation of two flights from London and Manchester.

The development came after Norse Atlantic, a long-haul budget carrier, said its financial situation is “critical” and it requires new financing to meet short-term liquidity needs and continue operating.

Norse Atlantic says financial situation ‘critical’ In October, PIA signed an ACMI (aircraft, crew, maintenance, and insurance) lease agreement with Norse Atlantic Airways to acquire two state-of-the-art Boeing 787-9 Dreamliners, one of which arrived in Islamabad on Nov 1.

stories.title: Bangladesh ties of 'great importance' to Pakistan, President and PM tell visiting parliament speaker
summary: Bangladesh Parliament Speaker Hafizuddin Ahmad on Wednesday met with President Asif Ali Zardari and Prime Minister Shehbaz Sharif in Islamabad, where the Pakistani leaders reaffirmed that Islamabad attached “great importance” to its ties with Dhaka.
The president expressed Islamabad’s desire to further strengthen parliamentary cooperation with Dhaka, as well as highlighted bilateral cooperation in the education and media sectors.

President Zardari welcomed progress under the China-Bangladesh-Pakistan Trilateral Mechanism, particularly the identification of 12 priority areas of cooperation during the Kunming meeting on June 19, 2025, the statement said.

stories.title: KP’s Karak reports 'first polio case in 6 years', taking countrywide 2026 tally to 10
summary: ISLAMABAD: The National Emergency Operations Centre for Polio Eradication (NEOC) has confirmed the country’s 10th paralytic polio case of the year, with the latest infection from Karak district in Khyber Pakhtunkhwa.
The country’s ninth polio case of the year was reported earlier this month, in KP’s Khyber district.
With the help of the vaccine and the efforts of hundreds of thousands of polio workers, Pakistan has reduced polio cases by 99.8pc since the launch of its national eradication programme in 1994.

stories.title: At least 3 killed, 14 injured after under-construction building collapses near Karachi's Baloch Colony
summary: KARACHI: At least three people were killed and 14 injured on Wednesday when an under-construction building collapsed in Karachi Administration Housing Society near Baloch Colony, according to police and rescue services officials.

Sindh CM directs SBCA to examine possible negligence, vows strict action Sindh Chief Minister Murad Ali Shah took notice of the incident and directed the relevant authorities to reach the site and expedite rescue operations, said a statement from the Chief Minister House.
The chief minister also directed the Karachi commissioner and relevant agencies to continuously monitor the rescue operation and submit a detailed report on the building collapse.

stories.title: NCCIA launches digital safety initiatives for Gen Z, kids and senior citizens
summary: ISLAMABAD: The National Cyber Crime Investigation Agency (NCCIA) on Wednesday launched three dedicated sections on its official website to promote cyber awareness among young people, children and senior citizens, in a bid to make them safe digital citizens.

Generation Z Cyber Zone The Generation Z Cyber Zone provides young people with complete awareness regarding online fraud, fake links, protection of personal information, responsible use of social media and other essential safety precautions, the statement said.

Cyber Safety Guide for Senior Citizens Senior citizens will be made aware of essential safety measures in an easy and understandable manner to protect themselves against fraudulent phone calls, deceptive messages, suspicious links and misuse of personal information.

stories.title: AJK Assembly sets conditions for resumption of dialogue with proscribed JAAC
summary: It alleged that JAAC had subsequently interpreted the government’s concessions and flexibility as weakness and raised unconstitutional demands incompatible with the existing constitutional and democratic structure of AJK.

The resolution warned that in case of non-compliance with its demands, the AJK government should discharge its constitutional responsibilities by taking necessary legal action through LEAs to restore state authority, maintain public order and protect citizens’ lives and property.

It resolved that political differences and public demands would be addressed through dialogue and constitutional means, but there would be no compromise on the rule of law, state authority and the protection of public life and property.

stories.title: At least 30 killed in blaze after vehicle overturns in Egypt, health ministry says
summary: At least 30 people were killed and 15 ​injured when a vehicle carrying petroleum ‌products overturned and caught fire on a major ring road in Egypt, the ​health ministry said on Wednesday.
The ​ring road connects key highways across ⁠Greater Cairo, linking the governorates of ​Cairo, Giza and Qalyubia.
Road accidents are common in Egypt due to ‌factors ⁠including speeding, weak enforcement of traffic regulations and poor road conditions.

stories.title: ‘A new era begins’: Pakistan’s Zeeshan Ali becomes first foreigner to board China's Tiangong space station
summary: Pakistan’s Zeeshan Ali on Wednesday became the first foreign astronaut to board China’s Tiangong space station, marking a historic moment for his country’s science ambitions and Beijing’s efforts to extend its space diplomacy.

The military leadership has congratulated the nation, the Suparco and the scientific community on the historic launch of Pakistan’s first astronaut to China’s Tiangong space station, the Inter-Services Public Relations (ISPR) said in a press release.

The ISPR said the journey of Zeeshan Ali, Pakistan’s first astronaut and the first foreign astronaut to travel to the Chinese space station, marked a defining moment in the country’s scientific and technological advancement and was a source of immense pride for the nation.

stories.title: Trump says he will meet 'smart guy' Abdul El-Sayed on universal healthcare
summary: Trump described El-Sayed as “a smart guy” and said he had done “a very good job” promoting the idea.
El-Sayed made universal healthcare a central issue in his campaign and sought to appeal directly to Trump by proposing that the plan carry the president’s name.
We can do a lot of great things together.” Trump repeatedly attacked El-Sayed during the campaign, while the Michigan Democrat was a vocal critic of the Trump administration.

stories.title: NCCIA claims busted call centre at Karachi's Sharea Faisal defrauding elderly US citizens
summary: The National Cyber Crime Investigation Agency (NCCIA) said on Wednesday that it had busted a call centre in Karachi for fraud, arresting five people and recovering Rs150 million in cash as well as about Rs60m in cryptocurrency.
According to a press release issued by the agency, the call centre allegedly defrauded elderly United States citizens with claims surrounding medical equipment and health insurance.
Earlier this month, the NCCIA claimed to have conducted a major operation against an alleged international fraud network and arrested 273 people from a call centre located on Sharea Faisal.

stories.title: Minister vows to upgrade GB's road infrastructure, reviews ongoing development work
summary: ISLAMABAD: Communications Minister Abdul Aleem Khan vowed on Wednesday to upgrade the road infrastructure of Gilgit-Baltistan (GB) to modern standards.
The minister said that the NHA had been directed to install lights along the Jaglot–Skardu Road, establish rescue services, and further enhance travel facilities for commuters.
The federal secretary for communications, NHA chairman and other senior officials briefed Aleem on the progress of various projects and apprised him of the challenges faced in their execution.

stories.title: US approves SpaceX plan to deploy one million data center satellites
summary: The US Federal Communications Commission (FCC) announced on Wednesday that it had authorised Elon Musk's SpaceX to deploy up to one million satellites designed to operate as data centers in space.

The authorisation, described by the agency as the first of its kind in US history, allows SpaceX to establish its Starmind constellation of orbital computing modules to process large amounts of data for use on Earth.
SpaceX first submitted its application for the orbital data centre network in January 2026, seeking permission to deploy as many as one million satellites.

stories.title: Mystery surrounds boat accident off Libyan coast as Bajaur families claim 25 deaths
summary: Several families across Bajaur were left shell-shocked and plunged into mourning after reports emerged that 35 local youths had died and several others were missing following a boat accident off the Libyan coast while attempting to reach Europe through illegal routes.
According to local sources, the victims' families said agents who had arranged their journeys abroad had informed them about the accident and the deaths of their loved ones.

Minister of State Mubarak Zeb Khan said he was in contact with the Pakistani embassy and officials of the Ministry of Overseas Pakistanis, adding that efforts would be made to repatriate the bodies and assist the affected families.

stories.title: Tarar urges social media companies to establish offices in Pakistan
summary: Federal Information Minister Attaullah Tarar on Wednesday urged social media companies to establish their offices in Pakistan and expand their presence in the country.

Social media platforms are paying you according to your [number of] views,” he said. “There is an algorithmic injustice,” he declared. “Social media has failed to protect the dignity and privacy of citizens,” the minister went on to say.
However, the government could not push social media companies to adhere to the laws of the country, Tarar said.

stories.title: US unveils proposed tariffs on major partners, including EU, China and India
summary: The United States on Wednesday unveiled proposed tariffs on 14 economies, including the European Union, China and India, after a months-long probe into alleged excess production — the latest move by US President Donald Trump to remake Washington’s trade relationships.
Trump’s latest duties come after an investigation the US Trade Representative started in March on excess manufacturing capacity and production.
For economies facing both the forced labour and excess production tariffs, the levies would not stack, the US official said.

stories.title: California grand jury indicts Meghan Markle's estranged father on child porn charges
summary: The estranged father of Meghan Markle, wife of Britain’s Prince Harry, was indicted by a California grand jury on Tuesday on two counts of possession of child pornography.

Thomas Markle, 82, who is already in custody in Florida after removing the ankle monitor that had been attached as a condition of house arrest, is expected to be arraigned in the United States District Court in Los Angeles in the coming weeks.
Meghan Markle said last month that she was “deeply distressed” by accusations that her father possessed images of child sexual abuse.

stories.title: AJK Assembly offers conditional talks with JAAC, demands disbandment of armed groups
summary: The resolution was unanimously adopted during a session chaired by AJK Legislative Assembly Speaker Chaudhry Tariq Farooq.

Read: AJK orders registration of all weapon licences within 10 days The House condemned the presence of armed groups, the closure of highways, attacks on government institutions and violence against law enforcement personnel.
According to the figures presented in the AJK Legislative Assembly, 34 law enforcement personnel were martyred and 248 injured during the unrest that began in June.

stories.title: JUI alleges arrest of Maulana Ghafoor Haideri, other party leaders by Punjab Police
summary: Jamiat Ulema-e-Islam-Fazl (JUI-F) spokesperson Aslam Ghauri on Wednesday alleged that party secretary-general Maulana Abdul Ghafoor Haideri had been arrested by Punjab Police, along with Punjab emir Maulana Amjad Khan and Jamiat Talaba-e-Islam (JTI) central president Malik Owais.

The development follows a series of events that have strained relations between the JUI-F and the government, including the withdrawal of security cover for JUI-F chief Maulana Fazlur Rehman and his son, Maulana Asad Mahmood.
The same day, party leaders condemned the withdrawal of security from Fazl and his son, Maulana Asad Mahmood, and alleged that police had cordoned off the JUI-F chief’s Islamabad residence.

stories.title: Senate body questions SECP over alleged fraud using Hum Network's name
summary: Read: Senate panel questions 'outdated' Pakistan Post operations SECP officials informed the committee that HUM Network was a listed company registered in 2004, with business interests in television programming and other sectors.
The committee decided to summon officials of the SBP, SECP and other relevant institutions at its next meeting to give a detailed briefing on the matter.
SECP officials told the committee that a letter had been sent to Hum Network seeking details of its Dubai-based entity and related bank accounts from HUM News Network.

stories.title: Raising our sons
summary: In Pakistan, rape is treated as a woman’s problem.
In Pakistan, rape is treated as a woman’s problem even though it is something men do, most often men she knows.
Government, media and advertisers could carry one national message, every day, not once a year: rape is a man’s choice and a man’s shame, and every man has a responsibility to speak up.

stories.title: Rawalpindiz secure Matthew Short as direct signing; Hyderabad Kingsmen opt out
summary: Rawalpindiz have confirmed the signing of Australian all-rounder Matthew Short as their marquee direct signing for the 12th edition of the Pakistan Super League (PSL), which is scheduled to run from March 18 to May 2 next year.
The 31-year-old, who captains Adelaide Strikers in the Big Bash League (BBL), becomes one of the highest-paid direct signings for the upcoming season.
Under PCB regulations, each franchise is permitted one direct signing of a marquee player who did not appear in PSL 10 or PSL 11.

stories.title: Govt slashes petrol by Rs4, diesel by Rs5 for Nov 26
summary: The federal government on Wednesday decreased the price of petrol by Rs4 per litre and that of high-speed diesel (HSD) by Rs5 per litre for November 26.
The latest revision comes a day after the government decreased the price of petrol by Re1 per litre and that of HSD by Rs4 per litre for November 25.

Read: Govt cuts petrol by Re1, diesel by Rs4 for Nov 25 On November 2, the government announced that oil refineries would bear a burden of Rs15 billion per month, which would allow petrol to be sold Rs15 cheaper than it was in the global market amid the US-Israeli war on Iran.

stories.title: £190m corruption case: Imran, Bushra's counsel says transaction caused no loss to exchequer
summary: ISLAMABAD: In the £190 million corruption case, counsel for PTI founder and former prime minister Imran Khan and his wife, Bushra Bibi, argued that the transaction had caused no loss to the national exchequer but had instead proved financially beneficial.
According to the prosecution’s case, Imran allegedly approved the transfer of the frozen funds to an account maintained by the Supreme Court in violation of the Rules of Business.

The prosecution had alleged that Riaz provided Rs285 million for the university’s building and furniture, but the amount was never transferred to Imran or Bushra’s personal accounts, the counsel argued.

stories.title: Pakistan reports 8th polio case from K-P as nationwide tally reaches 10 in 2026
summary: Pakistan on Wednesday reported its 10th polio case of 2026 after a 14-month-old girl from Karak district in Khyber-Pakhtunkhwa (K-P) tested positive for the virus, the National Emergency Operations Centre (NEOC) said.
Read: Pakistan reports ninth polio case of 2026 as virus spreads in K-P Among the eight cases reported in the province, four have emerged from southern K-P, it added.
Also Read: Karachi polio case takes Pakistan’s tally to seven this year It also appealed to all segments of society to play their role in efforts to eradicate polio from the country.

stories.title: India says 'cockroach' movement leader Das was told not to use passport
summary: India's foreign ministry said on Wednesday that passport authorities asked 'cockroach' movement leader Saurav Das not to ​use his passport until he clarified information about ‌his place of birth.
Das said on Monday he was stopped at Delhi airport hours before he was due to fly to London to address students, following a notice issued by passport authorities.

Das alleges passport leak by BJP-aligned social media accounts, vows legal action In a social media post on X, Das accused social media accounts aligned with PM Modi's BJP of leaking his passport details, saying he would file a criminal complaint against those involved.

stories.title: 'Let’s not blow it out of proportion': De Villiers urges cricket to move on from 'Sandpapergate'
summary: Former South Africa captain AB de Villiers said lessons must be learnt from the 2018 ball-tampering scandal involving Australia but urged the sport to move on from “Sandpapergate”.
And I think it affects the whole cricketing world, not just Australia,” De Villiers said. “We all want the game to be in a good position, right?

They need to clear it up completely and find a way for reverse swing to survive and still be around for many years to come. “I feel it’s part and parcel of the game, and it’s great for the bowlers to have that.

stories.title: National conference calls for stronger safeguards for freedom of expression, journalist safety and accountability
summary: The legislation drew widespread criticism from journalists, media organisations and rights activists, who argue that it undermined the fundamental right to freedom of expression.

The conference also underscored the need for sustained collaboration among policymakers, public institutions, media organisations and civil society to safeguard freedom of expression and create a safer, more accountable and financially sustainable media environment in Pakistan.

The report, titled “Regulatory Repression of Freedom of Expression – Legal Controls and PECA Undermine Media and Journalism in Pakistan”, identified the amended PECA as the most “consequential instrument” being used to restrict journalists and free speech practitioners.

stories.title: President Zardari calls for stronger Pakistan-Bangladesh ties, offers defence cooperation
summary: President Zardari stressed the need to deepen bilateral relations through educational links and people-to-people contacts, while reaffirming Pakistan's readiness to extend defence cooperation to Bangladesh.

Highlighting educational cooperation, the president referred to the Pakistan-Bangladesh Knowledge Corridor launched last year, which offers 500 fully funded scholarships to Bangladeshi students at leading Pakistani universities.
Also Read: Pakistan attaches great importance to its relations with Bangladesh: DPM Dar Discussing bilateral trade, Zardari observed that trade between the two countries remained below its potential.

stories.title: Trump unveils new tariffs to fight excess factory capacity, undeterred by midterms defeat
summary: His administration proposed new ‌headline tariff rates of 20% to 40%, but said duties would be capped at lower levels agreed under trade deals that have already been concluded or remain under negotiation.
Under the main "Section 301" probe into excess ​industrial capacity, China would face the highest capped rate of 20%, which would be added to duties of roughly 25% imposed during Trump's first ⁠term.

The U.S. has proposed new tariffs on 14 partners including China, the European Union, Japan and India, as President Donald Trump doubles down on levies, despite a large chunk of his previous duties being struck down by the Supreme Court.

stories.title: Fact check: Viral video of petals being showered on Sikh pilgrims is not from Guru Nanak’s 557th birth anniversary celebrations in Nankana Sahib
summary: Local digital media outlet Azaad Urdu also shared the same video captioned: “Pakistan’s unparalleled hospitality: Sikhs who came from India showered with rose petals from a helicopter.” Business Recorder also shared the same video on its Instagram account.

FACT-CHECK STATUS: FALSE The claim that a viral video shows a helicopter showering rose petals on Sikh pilgrims arriving from India for Baba Guru Nanak’s 557th birth anniversary celebrations in Nankana Sahib is false.
The video is old and shows a helicopter showering rose petals over Harmandir Sahib (the Golden Temple) in Amritsar, Indian Punjab, on October 28, 2023.

stories.title: Maldives national airline to start direct flights to Pakistan soon, meeting told
summary: Well-known Pakistani cricketers, artists and other celebrities will travel to the Maldives on the first direct flight, the meeting was told. “Pakistani celebrities are extremely popular in Maldives; their arrival will promote tourism,” the Maldivian minister said.
During President Muizzu’s visit, Prime Minister Shehbaz Sharif said he had issued instructions for direct flights between Pakistan and the Maldives.
The premier said he had been informed by President Muizzu that Muizzu had given instructions “to his airline to work out a quick plan to start flights from [the] Maldives to Pakistan”.

stories.title: PM approves NCCIA restructuring, orders overhaul of cybercrime prevention system
summary: ISLAMABAD: Prime Minister Shehbaz Sharif on Wednesday ordered the modernisation of the system to prevent cybercrime in the country and approved the restructuring of the National Cyber Crime Investigation Agency (NCCIA).
A meeting, presided over by the premier, was held to review the NCCIA’s performance, administrative structure and future strategy.

He also ordered the formation of a committee comprising Federal Ministers Mohsin Naqvi, Azam Nazeer Tarar, Muhammad Aurangzeb and Shaza Fatima Khawaja to review the reform proposals submitted by the NCCIA.

stories.title: Pakistan warns nuclear weapons must remain under 'human control', demands global AI guardrails to curb arms race
summary: On August 18, Pakistan assumed the presidency of the United Nations Conference on Disarmament in Geneva, placing Islamabad at the helm of the world's principal multilateral forum for negotiating arms control and disarmament treaties at a critical time for global security.
Pakistan is one of nine nuclear-armed countries, along with the US, Russia, China, France, the UK, India, North Korea and Israel.
The Stockholm International Peace Research Institute estimates that the nine countries hold a combined 9,745 nuclear warheads in their military stockpiles.

stories.title: Pakistan, China agree on government-to-government arrangements for fuel storage, terminal facilities
summary: ISLAMABAD: Pakistan and China agreed on Wednesday to pursue government-to-government (G2G) arrangements for Chinese investment in Pakistan’s petrol and liquefied petroleum gas (LPG) storage and terminal facilities, according to a Petroleum Division statement.

The minister also encouraged the Chinese side to advance investment across upstream, offshore, minerals, mining and downstream energy infrastructure, building on President Xi’s priorities announced at Apec 2026 in Shenzhen.

Opportunities in petroleum storage, terminals and wider downstream infrastructure were discussed, positioning PSO as the key commercial partner for Chinese investment in Pakistan’s downstream energy ecosystem.

stories.title: Jensen Huang's return to Nvidia fuels Washington fight over China's chip access
summary: US President Donald Trump's intervention to save the career of Nvidia CEO Jensen Huang might have settled the question of who would run the world's most valuable chipmaker, but it has only intensified Washington's bigger fight over artificial intelligence, chips and China.

But it worried some US officials and infuriated many lawmakers, both Democrats and some of Trump's fellow Republicans, who said Huang's return imperilled US security and called for tighter control of China's access to advanced chips used in artificial intelligence.

On ​the other are China hawks in Congress and some parts of the administration, who want to choke off Beijing's access to the advanced chips that power the leading AI models and that only Nvidia and AMD produce.

stories.title: ADB approves $250m to strengthen Pakistan’s PPP framework, attract private investment
summary: A statement issued by ADB said the financing will support government reforms aimed at preparing commercially viable projects, particularly high-quality and cost-efficient infrastructure, while improving the management of fiscal risks associated with PPP arrangements.

Another key component is the development of a national framework to monitor and disclose fiscal liabilities arising from PPP projects. “With ADB’s support, the government has also approved a medium-term PPP project pipeline covering 2026–2030,” the statement outlined.

The statement underscored that the technical assistance has helped strengthen institutional capacity and project preparation for federal PPPs through professional certification, knowledge exchange and the development of fiscal risk assessment tools.

stories.title: Eisenkot clinches first coalition agreement in bid to form Israel's government
summary: Israel’s Yashar party, led by former military chief Gadi Eisenkot, said on Tuesday it agreed to sign a coalition pact with a right-wing opposition party as it ​seeks to form a government following last month’s election.

Israel’s parliament was sworn in on Nov ​10 without a new government, after the election on Oct 27 stripped Prime ​Minister Benjamin Netanyahu of his majority but left others with no clear ⁠path to power.
But they have potential allies in the parties representing Israel’s ​Arab minority, which hold 19 seats and are aligned with Eisenkot in their vehement opposition ​to Netanyahu.

stories.title: Five held as NCCIA busts international medical billing fraud network in Karachi
summary: According to the Additional Director NCCIA Shahzad Akbar, the network allegedly targeted elderly citizens in the United States through fraudulent medical equipment offers and fake health insurance claims.
Investigators identified 23 bank accounts, mainly maintained at a private bank's SMCHS branch in Karachi, which were allegedly opened in the names of fictitious companies and firms.
In the latest case, the NCCIA said the alleged fraud proceeds were routed through fictitious business accounts and merchant facilities before being transferred to Pakistan.

stories.title: Bangladesh garment workers win 36pc wage rise
summary: Bangladesh’s garment workers won a 36 per cent minimum wage increase on Wednesday, officials said, after weeks of sometimes violent protests causing hundreds of millions of dollars in business losses.

The garment industry, which clothes millions of consumers across Europe and North America, is Bangladesh’s economic lifeline, generating four-fifths of export earnings and employing more than four million people.

The wage hike will take effect in January. ‘Export engine’ Bangladesh Garment Manufacturers and Exporters Association (BGMEA) said on Sunday that protests had cost the industry an estimated $428 million, while orders worth $254m had shifted to other countries.
